widgets_values:
UPSCALE SETTING

Try to get to about 1920 long edge so figure out the upscale settings from that. It will depend on your length whether your GPU can handle it without ooms.

my 3060 can do 24fps x 124 frames, to 1920 in about 11 mins. I adapt the multipler until it works for me. I've gone to 2048 or more on the long side before. Its known that 2mp is the best result but how much that influences low denoise runs is unknown.

widgets_values:
# INBOUND VIDEO SIZE:

This is where you will oom. so you need to find the sweet spot for your GPU between inbound video size and length of clip.

When you oom, then you need to reduce inbound video size until it fits or reduce the length of the clip.

If increasing inbound video size then I use the best Upscaler I have (RTX nvidia is fast), if I am reducing the inbound video size then I use Resize Image v2 from KJNodes, and set the height to 0, then the width controls the long edge and scales it.

## FRAME LENGTHS VRS ASPECT RATIOS VRS OOMS.

main oom culprit is length after aspect ratio. I fix that by changfing the "frame load cap" or "skip first frames" to get to what works if I dont want to change aspect ratio.

- 241 frames (10 seconds) with 1 image ref: I can do 1504 on long edge takes 20  mins. 3 image refs: 1334 on long edge takes 17 mins.

- 192 frames (8 seconds) best I got (1664 long size took 24 mins above it was oom) refer to video aspect rations notes over on the left for more info. 

- 124 is roughly 5 seconds and should be fine to 1920 long edge. mostly.

## Ultrawide screen (2.33:1)

1824 x 768 (1.4 mp)
1760 x 744 (1.31 MP)
1680 x 720 (1.21 MP) - 23 mins for 8 sec vid.
1280 x 576 (0.7 mp)
1216 x 512 (0.6 mp)
960 x 448 (0.4 mp) (1st pass, 2nd ends in 1920 x 896)

---

## 2.50:1 aspect ratio

or 2.50:1 equivalent (I was using with LTX for widescreen in "Black Magic" musical scenes. Its also faster than 16:9.)

1920 × 768 (1.47 MP)
1824 × 736 (1.34 MP) - 26 to 30 mins for 8 sec video (ooms often).
1760 × 704 (1.24 MP recommended)
1600 × 640 (1mp)
1440 × 576 pixels (0.83mp)
1280 x 512 (0.66 mp) - I start here usually for 5 secs
1120 x 448 (0.50 mp) - 
866 x 346 (0.3mp)
640 x 256 = (0.16mp) - test resolution 150 seconds.

# MarkDKBerry.com

YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry](https://www.youtube.com/@markdkberry)

Patreon: [https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies](https://www.patreon.com/c/AIMakingMovies)

Workflows: [https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows](https://github.com/mdkberry/comfyui_workflows)

---

This was adapted from a workflow by *"sftawil"* on Discord, and adapted here. Eventually removing the 1st sampler pass and using only the 2nd sampler as a detailer. This worked best of all my tests for detailed results. 

**WHY**? I think because using a fresh run means you are giving the Minimax model a new look at everything. This approach was superior to dual sampler methods I tried. So I will stick with it. It is also fast, considering.

**Updated**: 17th August 2026. *(As of 17th August this is by far the best detailer I have tested and the fastest.)*

**Use**: **SINGLE PASS LOW DENOISE v2v DETAILER USING MINIMAX H3**


---

## USING THIS WORKFLOW

**Get a structural video made elsewhere, then import it here for detailing.** I am finding 832 or 960 to be as big as it needs to be for structural round before importing here to resize.

**Set to Resize or Upscale the video** (see the notes beside the video import node). Resize if you need to reduce the inbound video, upscale if you need to increase it. Size it to fit your VRAM and avoid ooms.

**I've been leaving the width and height of the actual "H3 Reference To Video Model" Node set to 1mp**. We know it to be the size the H3 model was trained on. But the important bit is the size of your inbound video and what you resize that to.

**Set the length of the video in two places:** 1. the video frame count (inbound video node in frames) and match that in the "duration" node for the "H3 Reference To Video Model", *(even if you get this wrong it seems to still work)*.

**Length of clip vrs output resolution will be defined by where you OOM**. I have extensive notes for my 3060 RTX below, and how I set that is mostly based on clip length. That info is next to the "load video in" node. So use that as reference to figure out yours.

**Make a new prompt but target the ref images correctly**. **THEORETICAL ONLY:** If you made a prompt for MH3 when you first created the structural video, might want to do it differently here. i.e. maybe don't use the same prompt. I think giving it new information will help it detail the result better. This detailer approach as a seperate workflow instead of running it all in one with dual samplers, works better than any others I have seen. I don't yet know why. The results surprised me when I brought in a LTX video and detailed it with H3.

It's also faster. I am getting this done in 25 mins to higher resolutions, or longer clip length, due to the lower steps and denoise. Also reduce the number of media slots you use, this will help fight off OOMS and save on time to finish. But if reference accuracy is super important you may need all the slots, it will cost you in VRAM.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the blonde woman in <Picture 0>, with loose blonde hair, completely naked.
<Subject 2> is the brunette woman in <Picture 1>, with dark brown loose hair, completely naked.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video shows two women embracing sensually as the camera orbits around them. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> caress each other in an intimate embrace against a black background. The shot lasts 8 seconds with the camera slowly orbiting 360 degrees to the right while gradually moving in for an intimate close-up, ending with the women almost kissing as they have completed their full rotation.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - the blonde woman's appearance from <Picture 0>, including her loose hair and nudity, is retained throughout the video.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - the brunette woman's appearance from <Picture 1>, including her dark brown loose hair and nudity, is retained throughout the video.

detailed_description:
The target video uses a cinematic style with dramatic spotlight lighting against a completely black background. The scene features two women in an intimate embrace as the camera performs a slow orbital movement.
[Shot 1] the shot begins with <Subject 1>, the blonde woman with loose hair and no clothing, and <Subject 2>, the brunette woman with dark brown loose hair and no clothing, standing close together in an intimate embrace. They gently caress each other as the camera slowly orbits 360 degrees to the right around them. A spotlight from above creates dramatic shadows that shift subtly as the camera moves. The women maintain their sensual embrace throughout, their hands moving tenderly over each other's bodies. The background remains completely black throughout the entire shot.
[Shot 2] the camera gradually begins to move inward while continuing its orbital motion. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> remain locked in their intimate embrace, their faces turning toward each other as they caress one another more closely. The spotlight continues to cast dramatic shadows that shift with the camera's movement.
[Shot 3] the camera has moved significantly closer and is now transitioning into an intimate close-up. <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> are shown from the chest up, their faces inches apart as they almost kiss. The women have completed approximately two-thirds of their 360 degree rotation.
[Shot 4] the shot concludes with a tight close-up focused on <Subject 1> and <Subject 2>'s faces. They are intimately positioned as if about to kiss, having completed their full 360 degree turn around each other. The camera is now fully in close-up mode, capturing every subtle expression and movement of their intimate embrace. The spotlight continues to create dramatic shadows on their skin that shift with the final moments of camera movement.

overall_soundscape:
Silence throughout - no ambient sounds or environmental audio.

N/A
